title: Разговор по душам в кабинете  (A Heart-to-Heart in the Office)

segments.t: Impressed by Max's work at the stove, Aleksandr invites him into the office for a mid-shift drink and asks where he learned to cook. After joking that Max should have dodged the army too, the new chef starts asking which women at Claude Monet are single.
Спасибо, шеф.
Ты где готовить учился?
О, в армии еще чему-то учат?
А ты не служил?
Но, между прочим, тебе тоже надо было сбежать.
У тебя есть потенциал?
Да, заходи.
Да я вообще-то на работе.
Да ладно, шеф разрешает.
Слушай, а расскажи мне о наших девушках.
Понял, девушка моего друга, мой враг.
А ладно, в хорошем смысле.
А вон та.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
Спасибо, шеф.
'Thank you, Chef.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'thank you' and 'chef' in a few short words.
Ты где готовить учился?
'Where did you learn to cook?' Kostya raises the pitch on 'studied' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Nastya answers right away.
О, в армии еще чему-то учат?
'Oh, they still teach you something in the army?' The meaning hinges on 'about' working together with 'to learn' in spoken Russian.
А ты не служил?
'Wait, did you not serve?' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'and', while 'served' completes the thought.
Но, между прочим, тебе тоже надо было сбежать.
'By the way, you should have run away from the draft too.' Kostya addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'to escape'. Nastya answers right away.
У тебя есть потенциал?
'Do you think I have potential?' Nastya addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'potential'.
Да, заходи.
'Yes, come on in.' The grammar packs 'yes' and 'come in' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Да я вообще-то на работе.
'I am actually on the clock right now.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'yes' and finishing on 'work'. Nastya answers right away.
Да ладно, шеф разрешает.
'Come on, the Chef allows it.' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'really?!' in a few short words.
Слушай, а расскажи мне о наших девушках.
'Listen, tell me about our girls here.' The meaning hinges on 'listen' working together with 'young woman' in spoken Russian.
Понял, девушка моего друга, мой враг.
'Got it, pal's girlfriend is off-limits.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'understood?' and finishing on 'enemy'. Nastya answers right away.
А ладно, в хорошем смысле.
'All right, in the good sense.' Nastya anchors the line on 'and', while 'sense' completes the thought.
А вон та.
